newsitem.title: USA: Man sentenced for Russian scientist's ax murder.
newsitem.headline: Man sentenced for Russian scientist's ax murder.

text.p: The cousin of a woman convicted of the axe murder of her husband, prominent Russian scientist Yakov Gluzman, was sentenced on Thursday to 22-1/2 years in prison for helping with the brutal crime.
Vladimir Zelenin, 41, of Fair Lawn, New Jersey, had pleaded guilty to the charge in May 1996 and testified against his cousin, Rita Gluzman, during her January 1997 trial.
Zeledin was sentenced by U.S. District Judge Barrington Parker Jr. in White Plains federal court.
"You took a life in a callous and brutal fashion under circumstances it is impossible to rationally understand or justify, and can never be excused," Parker said.
The crime came to light when Zelenin was arrested on April 7, 1996, in East Rutherford, New Jersey, while emptying plastic bags containing Yakov Gluzman's body parts into the Passaic River.
Gluzman was found guilty of the murder of her husband, who was part of a team at Cold Spring Harbour Laboratory on Long Island credited with uncovering a genetic link to cancer in the 1980s.
Gluzman was the first woman to be tried under a federal law that was intended to stop vengeful men from travelling between states to commit domestic violence against women.

The Gluzmans were embroiled in a bitter divorce after a 26-year marriage marked by forced separation, political exile and then professional success after leaving the Soviet Union in the late 1970s for Israel and later the United States.
Prosecutors said Gluzman killed her husband because he filed for divorce and was planning to start a new life with another woman in Israel.
Prosecutors said Gluzman travelled from her $540,000 Upper Saddle River, New Jersey, home to the Pearl River, New York, apartment of her estranged husband, a molecular biologist.
There, she and Zelenin ambushed him. According to trial testimony the two cut their victim into more than 67 pieces and dumped the body parts into the Passaic River.
